comments.body:
> I have a fix that stops us from propagating the mma_layout through ReduceOps during the RemoveLayoutConversions pass; is this a fix you would accept or do you have any other guidance here?

This feels more like a workaround. It sounds like you have already narrowed down the bug quite a lot, it would be better to fix the bug instead. It sounds like it is something related to how mma layout are distributed along N dimension.

If you are not able to fix it maybe someone in the community can help, multiple people have helped fixing bugs around the codegen recently.

Yes it is a workaround, but it's also blocking the solution to another bug.  https://github.com/openai/triton/issues/2662 is caused because triton is currently not distributing wgmma instructions across all warps and we already have a solution here: https://github.com/openai/triton/pull/2956. Can I disable this very specific propagation (which currently isn't getting triggered at all right now), in favor of fixing the wgmma instructions?

I would only disable propagating the layout in this very specific scenario: where (1) it's a reduce op, (2) it's an mma layout and (3) the warps are spread across 2 dimensions.

And I will continue to look into the reduction issue as well, but I think using the correct wgmma instructions would be a nice improvement :)

> I would only disable propagating the layout in this very specific scenario: where (1) it's a reduce op, (2) it's an mma layout and (3) the warps are spread across 2 dimensions.

(2) could it be modified to ` it's an mmav3 layout`, if it's only triggered on hopper?

> Yes it is a workaround, but it's also blocking the solution to another bug. #2662 is caused because triton is currently not distributing wgmma instructions across all warps and we already have a solution here: #2956. Can I disable this very specific propagation (which currently isn't getting triggered at all right now), in favor of fixing the wgmma instructions?
> 
> I would only disable propagating the layout in this very specific scenario: where (1) it's a reduce op, (2) it's an mma layout and (3) the warps are spread across 2 dimensions.
> 
> And I will continue to look into the reduction issue as well, but I think using the correct wgmma instructions would be a nice improvement :)

I hear you, however I think upstreaming the workaround will be problematic. This is going to allow changing the heuristic to make the case you are looking faster but since we won't be able to propagate this layout through reduction this will make some other cases slower.

Most likely you've already the hardest part of the work by narrowing down the problem to a unit test and figuring out where is the bug shouldn't be very hard at this point (maybe @gflegar or others can help there)

How I see it is that we have 2 issues here:

1.  #2662 The mmav3 lowering is not correctly tiling the problem to all the warps that the user requested, and instead just assumes that the number of warps will be 4, and those will be tiled across block-rows, causing all other warps to be idle - this is solved in #2956.
2. #3467 (this issue) Reductions on mmav3 layouts that tile across columns produce wrong results.

I think it's better to have self-contained changes, so I would separate resolving (1) and (2) into 2 PRs.

Note that (2) only becomes a problem once (1) is solved, since before that it didn't make sense to tile across columns (the wgmma lowering just silently assumes this is not the case). We can:

- either just acknowledge that and submit the fix for (1) as is, or
- add a minimal workaround that Tori is describing above to ensure no one accidentally runs into the problem.

Both work for us, as long as we're not blocking (1) on fixing (2). 

We can then work on solving (2) and removing the workaround in a separate PR. **It won't make any other cases slower**, since no reasonable existing code would have even used column tiling as that would just cause idle warps. 

Would one of these options work for you?

> I think it's better to have self-contained changes, so I would separate resolving (1) and (2) into 2 PRs.

I agree those should be 2 separate PRs (they already are as far as I can tell)

> either just acknowledge that and submit the fix for (1) as is, or

I thought this was breaking tests?

> add a minimal workaround that Tori is describing above to ensure no one accidentally runs into the problem.

I still don't understand why we want to do the workaround as I don't think fixing the bug should be that complicated. 

> We can then work on solving (2) and removing the workaround in a separate PR. It won't make any other cases slower, since no reasonable existing code would have even used column tiling as that would just cause idle warps.

I'm not sure about that, I think in the context of a kernel with chained dots of different shapes it may happened. (that's just a guess I don't have proof)

> I thought this was breaking tests?

It was when TMA was involved but the code in question has been removed so not anymore :) I just rebased and it's  passing.

About the current issue: It can be replicated today from TTIR.

I created a test that fails from TTIR that proves this is an issue today without any other change: https://github.com/vwbaker/triton/commit/06e95caf42a8d921d31ebc385164375c76a16deb. Run the reproducer with `pytest test/unit/language/test_core.py -vvv -k 'test_reduce_layouts[max-float32-reduce1d-0-src_layout8-64-64]'`
The only thing that changed was to increase  BLOCK_N to be higher than the maximum instruction size so that all the warps would have necessary information.

About commenting out the normalization: I'm not sure why this is there; the test does pass with normalization, but it seems to be hiding a real issue by making the numbers "close enough" and making everything close to 0. When reduction is happening correctly as it is on the other tests, the tests pass just fine without the normalization.

I also printed out all the results that were > 1 because a softmax shouldn't have any values > 1 and there are a lot of values > 1 (~20%). And the numbers are all over the place from close to 0 to in the thousands so seems to be trash.

issue.body:
I am seeing that the MMA Layout for Hopper produces incorrect results on reduction, specifically when warps > 4 and distributed in 2 dimensions ([4,2] rather than [8,1]). I have a couple of minimal reasonable examples to play around with on `test_reduce_layouts` here: https://github.com/vwbaker/triton/commit/d6617967c0bd84a1000319a4bdaee4c9a04c7b7d. If you run this test (`pytest test/unit/language/test_core.py -vvv -k 'test_reduce_layouts[max-float32-reduce1d-0-src_layout8-64-64]'` ) against openai/main today, it fails with incorrect results.

Some context: I talked to @ThomasRaoux about this over slack a while ago, see conversation here: https://triton-lang.slack.com/archives/C01L894JD98/p1707416097320249?thread_ts=1707310247.070569&cid=C01L894JD98, but haven't had time to look more into it since then but am now looking into it again.

I have a fix that stops us from propagating the mma_layout through ReduceOps during the RemoveLayoutConversions pass; is this a fix you would accept or do you have any other guidance here?
issue.title: Reduction Op on MMA Layout produces incorrect results

issue.body:
This changes the `wgmma`  instruction shape based on the total number of warps.

Instead of always using the largest version of `wgmma`, it honors
the user's `numWarps` hint, and uses a smaller `wgmma` shape to
distribute the work to all warps, rather than having some of them
idle.

Using m's shape, it calculates how many warps will be used in the m
dimension, then see how many are left for the n dimension. Then, it
chooses the largest N such that it is still evenly distributed.
    
This resolves issue https://github.com/openai/triton/issues/2662.

issue.body:
Hopper forces a [0,1] order of warps for mma_v3 layouts
(https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#matrix-fragments-for-wgmma-mma-async-m64nnk8) while keeping a [1,0] order for threads so these two things have to be requested separately.

This resolves https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/issues/3467
